subject: URGENT: NovaBank - North America edge 502/503 spike impacting API calls
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novabank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: platform@novabank.com
Date: 2027-06-22T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: URGENT - North America API 502/503 spike

Marissa / Redwood team,

We're seeing a sudden uptick in 502/503 responses from the Redwood API in the US-West region starting ~07:50 PDT. Error rate is currently ~37% for our tokenization/embedding calls and latency has jumped from ~120ms to >1.8s. Our retry logic is kicking in and we're seeing cascading retries on our side. Attached a short capture (novabank_error_capture.zip) and a screenshot of the dashboards (screenshot_502.png).

This is impacting transaction processing for a subset of customers. Please advise ETA and what mitigation you can apply immediately.

-Elena
Elena Torres
Sr. Platform Ops, NovaBank
elena.torres@novabank.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novabank.com>
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-22T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT - North America API 502/503 spike

Thanks Elena — we see it and are triaging now. I've opened an incident and looped in SRE and infra. Initial ask: can you confirm if the spike correlates to a specific route or model_id? Any short curl sample or request id from your logs would help.

We're going to follow the live runbook (link below) and will provide an update in 15 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we'll prioritize this.

Runbook: https://drive.redwood.com/runbooks/edge-502-mitigation
Incident: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-789234

—Marissa Cole
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-22T08:28:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Initial SRE findings — US-West edge 502/503 burst

TL;DR: ALB in us-west is returning 502/503 due to backend connection resets and queue saturation. We see a correlated surge in requests-per-second from a small subset of customers starting 07:48. The shape looks like a retry amplification pattern (clients retrying on timeouts -> backend overloaded -> more timeouts).

Observations:
- ELB 5xx spike + increased backend 504 timeouts between 07:48-08:15.
- Backend CPU on model-inference pool a4-serve-usw-2 at 90%+, connection queue length growing.
- Several model containers reported long GC pauses and worker thread exhaustion.

Proposed immediate mitigations (implementing now):
1) Apply temporary token bucket rate-limit at edge for the affected route (200rps per-customer) to stop amplification.
2) Bring up warm standby pool (+3 nodes) and increase worker threads incrementally.
3) Enable regional fallback to a smaller model-variant (compatible but lower throughput) for non-critical routes.
4) Close the canary rollout flagged at 07:30 if it's contributing to hot shards.

I'll push commands and post updates here. Attaching short traces from the edge: edge_trace_0802.txt (included in zip).

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-22T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Mitigations applied (rate-limit + pool scale)

Actions taken at 08:36 PDT:
- Scaled up model-inference pool 'a4-serve-usw-2' by +3 nodes (added capacity).
- Applied edge rate-limit: 200rps/cust for route /v1/embeddings (token-bucket).
- Enabled fallback model variant 'embed-lite-v2' for non-SLA-critical calls via routing policy.
- Temporarily disabled canary traffic for model-id m-deploy-2027-06-22-07:30.

Quick log snippets:
[08:36:12] INFO scale: add_node node-238a -> OK
[08:36:28] INFO rate-limit: /v1/embeddings -> 200rps/cust applied
[08:37:03] INFO routing: fallback embed-lite-v2 enabled for route match 'X-NB-NonCritical'

Early result: 502/503 rate dropped from ~37% to ~9% at 08:45; p95 latency decreased from 1.8s to 350ms for primary flow (ongoing). Monitoring closely.

—Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novabank.com>
Cc: platform@novabank.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-22T08:56:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT - North America API 502/503 spike

Elena — thanks for the patience. We applied a short-term mitigation plan: rate limiting at the edge, scaled the backend pool, and enabled a fallback model for non-critical routes. Our metrics show error rates dropping substantially; we expect full recovery within 30 minutes as new nodes warm up.

Can you confirm whether any high-value transactions were affected so we can prioritize verification? We'll prepare a post-incident summary and root-cause analysis; I'm also escalating for account credits given the impact.

Apologies again — we'll follow up with a postmortem and longer-term fix plan (circuit breakers + smarter retry guidance) by EOD.

—Marissa Cole
Senior CSM, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai | marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@novabank.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, platform@novabank.com
Cc: ops@novabank.com
Date: 2027-06-22T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: URGENT - North America API 502/503 spike

Thanks — we can see partial recovery in our dashboards as well. A handful of payment tokenizations failed (we'll send ids separately). Please include our account exec for credit discussion and a formal postmortem with RCA and mitigation timeline. We'll need assurance that canaries and rollout controls won't cause shard hotness in the future.

Please escalate to our account team: contacts@novabank-sales.com.

-Elena
